 The Dallas Mavericks are coming into the 2026-27 season looking to continue on their current rebuild path centered around rising star Cooper Flagg. The team still needs to get in the good graces of the fanbase following the asinine Luka Doncic trade, and having a cornerstone like Flagg in the fold is a good way to do so. The No. 1 overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, he's a good candidate on the Mavericks roster to have a breakout season en route to a potential first All-Star selection.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement But Flagg is the obvious Mavericks player to be picked for a breakout season. There's also Dereck Lively, a lottery pick himself who has suffered unfortunate injury luck. If he's healthy, he could have a big year as well. But the one Mavericks player who seems destined for a breakout season is another former No. 1 overall pick in Zaccharie Risacher .
 Zaccharie Risacher on pace for breakout Mavericks season 
 Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images
 The jury is still out on the 2024 NBA Draft. It's been two years in with a mixed bag of results. Risacher, who was the No. 1 overall pick that year, has been underwhelming to this point. He actually had a rather solid rookie season with the Atlanta Hawks, even finishing second in the Rookie of the Year voting behind only Alex Sarr. But amid the expectations that come with being the top pick, it kind of went unrecognized.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) 
 But if the French native showed flashes of developing into a legit building block, Risacher's second year in the NBA was a major step back . His minutes dropped slightly from 24.6 to 22.4. His scoring dropped from 12.6 points to 9.6. His shooting percentages stayed relatively the same, however.
 But during the Hawks' opening round playoff series against the New York Knicks, his role and minutes were cut dramatically. He appeared in three games at slightly over seven minutes per game, and averaged only 3.7 points and 3.0 rebounds while shooting less than 40 percent from the field and less than 30 percent from the 3-point line.
 He was eventually traded to the Mavericks in the offseason in a multi-team deal. But so far, he's had a solid preseason with his new team.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Risacher started all four of the Mavericks' preseason games, at a little over 24 minutes per game. He averaged 12.2 points, 5.0 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.0 steals with splits of 48.9 percent shooting from the field, 17.6 percent shooting from the 3-point line and 66.7 percent shooting from the free-throw line.
 He closed the preseason with an 18-point performance in 27 minutes. He shot 8-of-12 from the field and also finished with five rebounds and four assists. Obviously his 3-point percentage could be cause for concern, but that's something that can be worked on.
 Click Here to Subscribe Mavericks head coach Dusty May was non-committal when asked if Risacher was going to remain in the starting lineup to open the regular season, as per Ron Harrod Jr. of DLLS Mavs, but did acknowledged that he would play a major role this year.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement This opportunity represents a fresh start for the 21-year-old. The longer he stayed with the Hawks, the more pressure he'd have upon him to perform like a No. 1 overall pick. With the Mavericks, alongside Flagg and given their current state, there is less pressure on him. He can play more freely and confidently. And it looks like he's already begun to do that if the preseason is any indication. He is without a doubt a strong candidate to shock the NBA world and have a breakout season for the Mavericks.
